notes: Source: 2026 Washington Commanders Media Guide (IA item washington-commanders-2026-media-guide-2026-08-20), HISTORY AND RECORDS section (opens p187). Individual records are on three sets of pages: RECORD BOOK - INDIVIDUAL pp. 268-279 (three-column boxes: value | player | years or date; top 3, a few lists longer), RECORD BOOK - TOP 10 (CAREER) pp. 280-283 (tables with printed ranks such as '1.' and '2t.', t = tied) and RECORD BOOK - SINGLE SEASON pp. 284-286 (same style). Printed page numbers are PDF page minus 1 (PDF p280 prints 279, PDF p286 prints 285); pdf_page in this file is the PDF page.

Franchise scope: the record book covers the whole franchise under all names, including the Redskins years back to the 1930s (Cliff Battles 1932-37, Sammy Baugh 1937-52, Charley Taylor 1964-77, Art Monk 1980-93 and so on) and the Commanders years; p226 'IMPORTANT DATES' opens with the club's start in 1932.

through_season is 2025: the lists contain 2025 entries (Terry McLaurin 2019-25 on the career receptions list, Daron Payne 2018-25 and Tress Way 2014-25, Jaylin Lane 2025, Matt Gay vs. LV Sept. 21, 2025 on the field goal list p269) and the guide is the 2026 edition (dated 2026-08-20).

Which list was used: for each category the longest list ranked by the exact stat. Career passing/receiving/rushing-TD/sacks lists come from the TOP 10 (CAREER) tables; the guide has no career rushing-yards table there, so career rushing yards (3 rows) come from the INDIVIDUAL box. Season passing, receiving, sacks and interceptions come from the SINGLE SEASON tables; season rushing (yards and TDs) and all game lists come from the INDIVIDUAL boxes. Where a stat is printed on two pages the top rows agree (checked: top 3 of career passing yards, passing TDs, receptions, receiving yards, receiving TDs and sacks since 1982; top 4 of career rushing TDs; top 3 of season passing yards, passing TDs, receptions and receiving yards; the season receiving TDs top 5); the only difference found is Coy Bacon 1979 in the INDIVIDUAL season sacks list (see below).

Two career sacks lists are printed and both are included as separate lists: 'Sacks (Since 1982)' (official sacks only; the list the TOP 10 page uses) comes first and 'Most Sacks, Career (Unofficial)' (all years, Manley 97.5) second; both are the guide's own, only the first has ten rows. Season sacks use the SINGLE SEASON list, which leaves out Coy Bacon 1979 (15.0, a pre-1982 unofficial season) that the INDIVIDUAL 'Most Sacks, Season' list (18.5, 15.0, 15.0) prints; the game sacks list has no qualifier but includes Diron Talbert 1975.

Flagged rows (uncertain: true): career passing yards rows 9 and 10 (Norm Snead 8,306 printed above Robert Griffin III 9,097, so one number or the order is wrong in the guide); season receiving TDs second McLaurin '2024' row (the same player-season appears with 13 and 11); the single row for game receiving TDs (aggregate '20 Times, last Santana Moss'). The one warning the validator prints (career passing yards, value rises at row 10) is that misordering: the digits were checked at 400 dpi and by an independent OCR.

Ties: every tied row has tie=true; the TOP 10 and SINGLE SEASON tables print 't' after the tied rank ('2t.'), the INDIVIDUAL boxes print no ranks so rank = printed position with tied values sharing the lowest rank. 'complete_to' is the number of rows the guide prints for that list (not only the rows copied: all printed rows were copied).

Game lists: 'years' holds the printed date as M/D/YYYY plus the printed opponent as printed ('vs. PHI', 'at SF'); raw keeps the printed text. The bracketed number after an opponent in the receiving-yards list ([7], [11]) is receptions in that game and is kept in raw only. 'Sammy Baugh at Dodgers' (Oct. 31, 1943) is printed that way (a Brooklyn Dodgers game). A career span printed with a gap, such as John Riggins '1976-79, 1981-85', is kept as printed.

Name spellings are as printed: 'Pierre Garçon' (with the cedilla), 'Roy Helu, Jr.', 'Robert Griffin III', 'Marco Coleman' (season sacks 2000), 'Laveranues Coles'. Asterisks on Dexter Manley's *91.0 and Monte Coleman's *43.5 in the career sacks list are unexplained on the page and kept in raw only. Rookie marks '[R]' (Dan Sandifer 1948, Paul Krause 1964 on the interceptions list) are in raw only.

Missing: no career or game interceptions list, no tackles list of any scope, and no player single-game rushing-touchdowns list exist in the guide (details in missing). The 'Most Touchdowns, Game' box (p268) counts all touchdowns and was not used for rushing.

Verification: every digit used was read from 200-dpi crops of the page pictures (the Snead/Griffin rows again at 400 dpi); the Internet Archive OCR text of these table pages drops most of the numbers, so it was not usable as a check. Instead a separate Tesseract run on border-cleaned 200-dpi renders matches 152 of the 176 rows verbatim (including the out-of-order 8,306 / 9,097 passing-yards rows) and the other 24 differ only by OCR noise (for example '27' read as 'a7', '2012-17' as '201247', 'Garçon' without the cedilla). Dates and values of the top rushing games (Riggs, Battles, Rogers) and passing games (Johnson, Cousins twice) also agree with the MILESTONE GAMES tables on pp. 237 and 240; the one difference is that George Rogers' 206-yard game of 12/21/1985 is 'vs. ARI' in the INDIVIDUAL box but 'at St. Louis' (the same Cardinals) on p237.
